title: Micro-deal Accelerator: one-pager + battlecard sketch
body:
Purpose: fast reference for selling small/early-stage proofs where buyer wants a quick hit (1-2 week pilot, low spend) and an engineer in the room. This is a compact one-pager that pairs a 3-slide demo flow with a two-column battlecard for objections and technical fit checks. Use when AE/SE have <=30 minutes with buyer and need to close on pilot commitment or signature for reserved capacity trial.

Target personas:
- Integration engineer / platform engineer (primary)
- Product manager / AI PM (secondary)
- Procurement lead (occasionally)

Elevator (30s):
Redwood gives predictable, low-latency inference that scales from sandbox to reserved capacity without swapping your integration. For pilots we provide an engineer-led demo, a low-risk reserved capacity trial, and a fallback plan so you can ship features quickly while keeping unit costs under control.

Quick value bullets (for slide 1):
- 5–15ms median token latency (demo config) on typical convo workloads
- Transparent per-token economics + batch suggestions tailored to your traffic shape
- Canary and fallback routing: keep product online if primary model becomes unavailable
- Enterprise-ready controls for data isolation in short pilots

Slide-by-slide demo outline (speaker notes):
Slide A: "Why this pilot?" (1 min) - Show product scenario + metric to improve (e.g., improve NPS for support triage, reduce triage time by 40%). Call out expected token volumes and latency SLO. Ask: "What success metric should we commit to for a 2-week pilot?"
Slide B: Live integration + meters (8–12 min) - Run a constrained demo of host API call, show latency stream, cost meter, and small heatmap of token distribution. If time limited, show a recorded trace. Highlight routing fallback and cost-breakdown.
Slide C: Runbook & asks (2–3 min) - Recommend pilot params (qps target, sample prompt set, SLAs), contract ask (trial credits + one-month reserved capacity at X% discount), and next steps.

Two-column battlecard (for quick reference during convo):
Buyer concern / objection -> Quick rebuttal / evidence -> SE play
- "We already use a hosted API (X)." -> "Redwood matches host-level ease plus reserved capacity and private mode for compliance; we can show transparent token metrics vs their receipts." -> Show side-by-side cost/latency snapshot; propose 1-week parallel POC.
- "Latency spikes in peak traffic." -> "Autoscaling + burst policy + routing to model variants keeps tail latency bounded; show canary trace." -> Pull up last-week dashboard for similar customer (anonymized) and show fallback in action.
- "We can’t share data to third parties." -> "Private deployment or VPC options and KMS integrations; playbook for air-gapped evals." -> Offer a checklist for minimal data transfer and signed NDA.
- "We need deterministic output quality/consistency." -> "Pin model versions + rollout canary and regression alerts tied to your prompt evals." -> Offer to run an evaluation harness on a seeded prompt set during pilot.

Technical fit checklist (quick tick-list for SE):
- Language(s) required: ___
- Max seq length expected: ___
- QPS / concurrency target: ___
- Token distribution (median/95p) observed: ___
- Need for on-prem/VPC/KMS: yes/no
- Required logging/PII retention controls: yes/no
- Integration time budget (engineer hours): 4/8/16+

Pricing & commitment ask (script):
- Pilot ask: 2-week sandbox + engineer support (4 hours), $X credits or reserved node for the window.
- Close ask: convert to 3-month reserved capacity at Y% discount with SLA, or stay hosted with committed monthly spend.

Demo script snippets (quick copy/paste lines):
- "Start live trace" command: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <demo-key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-psi-small","input":"<sample prompt>"}' (show latency/time-to-first-byte)
- "Cost peek" phrase to show: "This invocation used ~120 tokens; cost = $0.00X; batchable with 50% savings if queued to 200ms max latency"

Fallbacks & risk mitigations to highlight (keeps deal alive):
- Canary fallback to smaller/faster quantized model on capacity pressure
- Region fallback when primary region has degraded networking
- SLO-triggered auto-routing and customer notification hooks

Quick play tips (notes to AE/SE):
- Always ask for an engineering contact who can run a sample request within 48 hours.
- Bring an anonymized dashboard trace from a similar customer to lower friction.
- If buyer balks at price, pivot to cost-per-conversation framing and batching levers to show how unit economics improve.

Open questions / TODO (keep visible in doc):
- Define standard pilot credit levels for "micro" (suggested: $2k / 2-week) - finance approval needed.
- Create a one-click demo key provisioning path for AE portal (JIRA-PRIORITY).
- Collect 2 anonymized traces from top-3 similar customers for SE demo library.

Attachments & artifacts to assemble (for finalizing):
- one-slide price comparator (hosted vs reserved vs private)
- 3 sample dashboard traces (low/medium/high token mixes)
- short video: "engineer-led 8-minute micro pilot" (screen recordings)

Closing CTA (for slide C):
"Can we get a single integration test call from your engineer this week? If yes, we’ll provision a two-week pilot plan and ship a signed SOW template for the trial by EOD."

Notes (formatting for handoff):
- This doc is intentionally terse — make a copy per vertical (support bots, search re-rank, summaries).
- Keep a running list of objections we see; update the two-column battlecard weekly.

---
Internal status: rough sketch. Use in playbook sessions and iterate with SEs next week.
